name: Matthias Hartsell
languages: Church Latin (enough for a funeral; his mother wanted him to be a priest of some kind)
equipment: Heavy overcoat, charcoal wool, bought second-hand from a Pullman porter who was a bigger man
.38 revolver (Colt Police Positive), 6 rounds loaded, in a shoulder holster
Blackjack, braided leather, in the inside pocket where a wallet would go
Private investigator's license, State of Missouri, renewed in a fight every year
Lock picks in a chamois roll
Fedora, brown, with a feather he keeps meaning to take out
Business cards (100): MATTHIAS HARTSELL, CONFIDENTIAL INVESTIGATIONS, 18TH STREET, over Dandridge's
A ring of eleven hotel pass keys from his years at the Lincoln Arms and two other houses, most of which still work
Keys to the office over Dandridge's Barber Shop
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin: Kansas City, Eighteenth Street in particular; he knows which alleys go through and which bars, barbershops and pool halls belong to whom; advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city)
Hunch (Private Eye: once per short or long rest, ask the GM one yes-or-no question about a lead he has personally encountered in this case and get a true answer)
Gumshoe (Private Eye: proficiency bonus doubled for Investigation and Insight checks)

Size Them Up (Private Eye, 2nd level: as a bonus action, study one creature within 60 ft; his next attack against it this turn has advantage and deals an extra 1d6 damage on a hit; twice per short rest, his WIS modifier)
Specialty: Shamus (Private Eye, 3rd level: Hunch can be used twice per short rest, and once per long rest he can ask 'who?' about a single event instead, getting a name or 'nobody you've met')

Pass Key (Hotel Dick background: in any hotel he can get the house detective, night manager or a bellhop to tell him which room a guest is in and who visited, and he can get into a room without the desk knowing; he can spot a false name across a lobby)

personality.traits: I sit with my back to the wall and my hat on the desk and I let people talk until they run out. I remember faces, room numbers and what a man ordered for breakfast in 1927. I am polite to everybody, which on Eighteenth Street is good manners and downtown is armour.
personality.ideals: Everybody on this street is somebody. If the city won't look for them, somebody has to.
personality.bonds: Eighteenth Street, which raised me, and Mr. Dandridge, who rents me the office for less than it's worth and tells me so every month.
personality.flaws: For eleven years I was the house detective at a hotel that would not let me eat in its dining room, and I was good at it, and I was grateful. I am still angry about the gratitude.

appearance: A compact, neat Black man of forty-six with close-cut greying hair, a clipped moustache, careful brown eyes behind steel-rimmed reading glasses he takes off to look at people, and a way of sitting very still. A charcoal overcoat too big in the shoulders, a brown fedora, shoes polished by Mr. Dandridge's boy every morning whether they need it or not.
backstory: Matthias Hartsell was born on Highland Avenue in 1890, the son of a Pullman porter and a laundress, and has lived within six blocks of Eighteenth and Vine almost all his life. At twenty-five he went to work as a house detective for a downtown hotel, the only kind of police work a Black man could do there, watching the service corridors, the kitchens and the staff, never the guests. He was the best they ever had and they paid him half what they paid the white house dick on the lobby floor. In 1926 he moved to the Lincoln Arms on Eighteenth Street, where he could watch the front door too, and in 1933 he took out a private investigator's licence on his savings and opened an office over Dandridge's. He finds missing husbands, runaway daughters, stolen instruments and insurance frauds, mostly for people who cannot go to the police, and he has learned to be paid in chickens. He has known Jules Ransom since Jules came up from Oklahoma in 1925, a skinny boy with a cardboard suitcase who played the Lincoln Arms' lobby piano at four in the morning until the night manager told Matthias to throw him out, and Matthias sat down and listened instead. When Geneva Hollins comes up the stairs with forty dollars in a cigar box, he is going to take it, and he is going to find Jules, and he has already noticed the green Ford.
